---
title: "The silo problem"
description: "Three silos, no shared key — unified with entity resolution and scored against a hidden ground truth."
---

## Three silos that cannot talk to each other

The simulated marketplace's data is deliberately fractured the way real
marketplace data fractures:

| Silo | System | Grain | Identity scheme |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Auction lake | S3, partitioned Parquet | one row per bid event | `lead_uuid` (UUIDv4) |
| CRM | Neon Postgres | one mutable row per lead | integer `lead_id` + hashed email |
| Marketing | BigQuery exports | one row per message | `contact_id` (MD5 of lowercased email) |

No silo contains another silo's key, and the fracture injects the defects
that make real unification hard: about 8% duplicate consumers (nickname vs.
legal name, typo'd emails, new phone numbers), about 5% orphaned auction
events from a simulated migration, timestamps logged in three different
timezones (UTC, naive US/Pacific, US/Eastern), and "conversion" meaning three
different things in three systems. Each pathology is parameterized in the
[simulation engine](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/tree/main/simulation),
not hand-waved.

The consequence: before unification, nobody can say what a lead sold for
end-to-end, how many distinct consumers exist, or what revenue marketing
drove. The [before/after dashboard](dashboards.qmd) walks through nine such
questions.

## The trick that makes it measurable

The simulator generates every consumer with a true `consumer_key`, strips it
from all three silos, and keeps it in a private crosswalk that never enters
the cloud. The unification pipeline works blind, exactly as a real team
would — and is then *scored* against the crosswalk. Every claim below is a
measurement, not an assertion.

One honest note on difficulty: the pathology dials were deliberately tuned so
entity resolution lands in the 0.8–0.9 F1 band. Early versions of the
fracture were too clean and the matcher saturated — a synthetic benchmark you
can ace is not a benchmark.

## How the unification works

- **Probabilistic matching where it belongs.** CRM deduplication and the
  CRM-to-marketing link are [Splink](https://github.com/moj-analytical-services/splink)
  models (term-frequency-adjusted comparisons over name, email, phone,
  geography) — the classic fuzzy-identity problems.
- **Deterministic SQL where a model would obscure the truth.** The
  auction-to-CRM linkage is an exact composite key (state, loan amount,
  purpose, FICO band) plus a nine-minute submission window, choosing
  nearest-in-time. The residual errors are payload doppelgangers inside the
  window — which no probabilistic model could separate either, so the honest
  tool is the simple one. It also has to absorb a daylight-saving fall-back
  hour where CRM timestamps land 3,600 seconds off.
- **High-precision clustering.** Consumer entities are connected components
  over dedupe pairs at the 0.9 threshold, where pairwise precision is 0.9998
  — transitive closure amplifies any false edge, so clustering runs at the
  high-precision operating point rather than the F1-optimal one.
- **A thin dbt spine.** Two intermediate models map every lead and auction
  event to its resolved consumer entity; wide denormalized marts join through
  that spine.

## The scorecard

Scored against the hidden crosswalk
([er/scorecard.json](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/er/scorecard.json)):

| Task | Precision | Recall | F1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CRM–marketing link (probabilistic, best match per lead) | 0.895 | 0.864 | **0.879** |
| CRM dedupe (probabilistic, pairwise) | — | — | **0.873** |
| Auction–CRM linkage (deterministic) | 0.995 (lead) | 0.998 (non-orphan) | — |

Downstream identity quality: 636,164 resolved consumer clusters against
623,470 true persons, weighted cluster purity 0.9998, and 98.1% of persons
kept whole (unsplit).

**The headline:** 95.3% of auction events are consumer-joinable after
unification, against a >95% target and 0% before — and of the 4.7% gap,
almost all is the ~5% migration-orphan population that is unjoinable by
construction. The linkage recovers 99.8% of what is recoverable.

## What the unified view immediately paid for

- The CRM's 2.40M lead ids resolve to **635,579 actual consumers** — a 3.8x
  overcount; 69% of applications are repeat applicants.
- Buyers paid **$12.0M (5.7% of revenue)** for consumers they had already
  bought within the prior 30 days — invisible when every application looks
  like a new person.
- **93% of $209.2M** in revenue became attributable to a marketing
  touch, exposing paid-channel ROAS ranging from 0.94x (below break-even)
  to 3.06x.

All three, with charts, in the [dashboards](dashboards.qmd).
